headline: Bank of Korea Warns Chip Exports Could Drop by $100 Billion if AI Spending Slows
summary: The Bank of Korea modelled a pessimistic scenario warning that South Korea's semiconductor exports could fall by up to US$100 billion if artificial intelligence spending slows down.
why: Semiconductors constitute a massive share of South Korea's total exports, making the domestic economy highly sensitive to global technology capital expenditure cycles.

impacts.name: Semiconductors & Technology
impacts.why: Potential slowdown in AI infrastructure spending threatens heavy export losses for memory chip makers.

why_moved: A downturn in global artificial intelligence capital expenditure directly reduces overseas demand for high-end memory chips produced by South Korean manufacturers.
